cs.t: I worked like this for two years:  http://www.dqd.com/~mayoff/images/alfa.jpg  (picture shows the guy I got the idea from, not me) the backsaver zero-gravity line is not as flashy as the one in TFA but it allows locking the recliner at any angle you want, not just 3 pre-set ones. A backsaver will run $1000+ new, and the one in the TFA is probably more; if you want to try the idea out you can get a cheap lawn chair version for $65 on Amazon:  http://www.amazon.com/Strathwood-Anti-Gravity-Adjustable-Rec...  (I've tried that one too, and IMO it's a great value, although even more limited to "reclined" and "not reclined"). I stopped coding in a recliner since it was too hard to add a 30" monitor to the setup in a cubicle environment.
cs.th: Forget Aeron, here's the best programmer's chair in the world
